## 1. Executive summary
Bronx County, NY is a high-exclusion urban county with about 217,454 underserved households (modeled) and a poverty rate of 27.8%. We propose a 12-month pilot with a community issuer to test a Second-chance account offering clear rules and a path to a standard account. The pilot targets measurable reductions in account-closure complaints and improved account usage.

## 2. Why this area
Bronx County has an exclusion index of 92 and an underserved rate of 40.7%. Median household income is $48,676, no-internet rate is 9.6%, and there are 2.36 branches per 10,000 households, indicating limited physical access. State FDIC unbanked and underbanked rates are 5.1% and 15.4% respectively.

## 3. What frustrates people here and the benefit
Top complaints: account closures (pain 1.256) and customer service (pain 1.074). Matched benefit: Second-chance account — an account for people previously closed out of banking, with clear rules and a path to a standard account. Pilot will track account-closure complaints per 100k residents as the primary pain measure.

## 4. Offer design
- Product: Second-chance account with staged remediation milestones and explicit criteria to upgrade to a standard account.  
- Pricing and economics are simple: annual margin per account $69, swipe revenue $208, deposit earnings $42, fraud loss $7, servicing $175.  
- Targeted scale for Bronx: about 6,524 accounts (modeled) in year one; adoption assumption 3.0% (placeholder).  

## 5. Outreach plan
- Partners: Community credit union (TBD) and local community organizations only.  
- Channels: in-person enrollment through partner orgs, outreach materials at partner sites, and partner-led group sessions.  
- Compliance: issuer partner review of all outreach materials and processes. Outreach only through community organizations; no protected-attribute targeting; eligibility and outreach use economic access only.

## 6. Why Mastercard
Mastercard provides network reach and measurement capability without holding accounts, enabling rapid partnership with a community issuer and community organizations to reach underserved households and measure network spend impact.

## 7. Economics and the two levers
- Unit economics today: acquisition cost per account $428, lifetime value per account $172, net per account -$256, yearly churn 40.0%, breakeven churn 16.1%. Issuer net lifetime modeled -$1,743,618.  
- Network-level impact: network volume year 1 modeled $96,748,310 and network revenue year 1 placeholder $280,570; network yield placeholder 0.3%. Fixed program cost placeholder $75,000.  
- Two levers to move economics: reduce churn toward breakeven (from 40.0% toward 16.1%), and lower acquisition cost via trusted community partners and co-delivery.

## 8. Pilot design and success measures
- Geography: launch in Bronx County, NY with five look-alike counties for comparison: Broome, Monroe, Erie, Onondaga, Niagara.  
- Timeline: 12-month baseline, 12-month pilot with a 6-month read; difference-in-differences against look-alikes.  
- Scale: about 6,524 pilot accounts (modeled).  
- Primary measures: new accounts per 1,000 adults, 90-day active rate, transactions per account per month, yearly churn versus breakeven (16.1%), and target-topic complaints per 100k residents versus look-alikes.  
- 2x2 read: usage up + pain down = scale; usage up + pain flat = rework benefit; usage flat + pain down = fix outreach; both flat = drop.

## 9. Risks and safeguards
- Complaint data skews toward banked customers; complaints count is 2,122 and 151.1 per 100k residents, which may undercount unbanked experiences.  
- Underserved households are modeled from state FDIC rates and county poverty; about 217,454 underserved households (modeled).  
- Benchmarks for servicing are older; issuer partner required to operate accounts and bear compliance, fraud, and servicing risk. Safeguards: partner compliance review, limited initial scale, and complaint monitoring.

## 10. Decision needed
Approve the pilot and commit $75,000 (fixed program cost placeholder) to launch with a community issuer and community organization outreach.
